title: Distributed agency in second language learning and teaching through generative AI
extended_summary:
This paper is a theoretical and position-oriented discussion of how generative AI is reshaping second language learning and teaching. It asks how agency is distributed among learners, teachers, and AI systems, and argues that AI should be understood not simply as a tool but as an active participant in language-learning ecologies.

The article surveys current and emerging uses of generative AI such as ChatGPT for language practice, corrective feedback, lesson-plan creation, writing support, assessment, and immersive learning. It emphasizes critical AI literacy, describing why learners and teachers need to understand both the capabilities and limitations of large language models. The paper also discusses ethical concerns, bias, inaccuracies, pragmatic limitations, and unequal access, especially for less privileged users.

The context is broadly instructed second language education rather than a single empirical site or intervention. The author draws on ecological theories, sociomaterialism, and relational pedagogy to frame AI-human interaction as shared and distributed agency. The main conclusion is that AI can support learning and teaching, but only when used critically, ethically, and with awareness of sociocultural limitations, power relations, and the need to preserve human agency and multilingual, context-sensitive language use.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/emerging-technologies column rather than an empirical study. It synthesizes prior work and offers theory, examples, and cautions, but does not present a defined study design, comparison, or original outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No original effect estimates or outcome data are reported, so there is no measurable impact to classify. The paper is useful as a theoretical overview of benefits and risks, but not as evidence of effectiveness.

interventions.use_case: generative AI chatbots and custom GPT-style tools used for second-language practice, conversational interaction, prompt-based feedback, and teacher-created AI-assisted language learning materials
AI-assisted writing support for L2 learners, including grammar checking, style improvement, translation, brainstorming, drafting, revision, and customized prompt-based writing feedback
AI-generated corrective feedback and rubric-based feedback on student writing, including individual text analysis and suggestion of revisions
